test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 3 Feb 2022)
subject: general
question: A solid metallic sphere of radius 4 cm is melted and recast into spheres of the radius of 2 cm each. What is the ratio of the surface area of the original sphere to the sum of surface area of the spheres, so formed?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Number of spheres (n) = (Original Radius ÷ New Radius)³ = (4 ÷ 2)³ = 2³ = 8

Surface Area Ratio = Original Area : (n × New Area)

Ratio = R² : (n × r²) = 4² : (8 × 2²) = 16 : (8 × 4)

Ratio = 16 : 32 = 1 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of original sphere (R) = 4 cm

Radius of small sphere (r) = 2 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of sphere = (4/3) × π × radius³

Surface area of sphere = 4 × π × radius²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b520bda9d2763b0c69982ef444661a09b4f40745dc53a207268f856f3dd7790.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total volume remains constant during melting.

⇒ Volume of original sphere = n × Volume of small sphere

⇒ (4/3) × π × 4³ = n × (4/3) × π × 2³

⇒ 64 = n × 8

⇒ n = 8

⇒ Surface area of original sphere (SA₁) = 4 × π × 4² = 64π cm²

⇒ Sum of surface areas of 8 small spheres (SAₜₒₜₐₗ) = 8 × (4 × π × 2²)

⇒ SAₜₒₜₐₗ = 8 × 16π = 128π cm²

⇒ Required Ratio = SA₁ : SAₜₒₜₐₗ = 64π : 128π

⇒ Ratio = 1 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Conservation of Volume

When a solid is melted and recast into other shapes, the total volume remains constant (Vᵢₙᵢₜᵢₐₗ = Vfᵢₙₐₗ).

Sphere Properties

For a sphere of radius R: Volume = (4/3)πR³ and Total Surface Area = 4πR².

Ratio of Dimensions

If the ratio of radii of two spheres is a:b, then the ratio of their surface areas is a²:b² and the ratio of their volumes is a³:b³.</p
